groundnut.rationale: Groundnut + Pigeonpea (7:1 row ratio) is an ICAR benchmark dryland system; shallow groundnut canopy pairs with deep-rooted pigeonpea.
Groundnut + Castor provides windbreak barrier protection, diverts leafminers, and enhances temporal water utilization.
Groundnut + Sunflower (6:2 ratio) improves solar radiation capture and provides pollinator nectar synergy.

soybean.rationale: Soybean + Pigeonpea (4:2 row ratio) utilizes differential growth durations (90d vs 180d) with zero inter-row competition.
Soybean + Maize pairs C3 legume nitrogen fixation with high-radiation C4 cereal photosynthesis.
Soybean + Sorghum (4:2 ratio) suppresses weeds and mitigates early-season dry spell risks.

finger_millet.rationale: Finger Millet + Pigeonpea (8:2 or 10:2 ratio) is the classic Karnataka dryland standard optimizing vertical canopy tiers.
Finger Millet + Cowpea provides rapid green soil cover, biological nitrogen fixation, and soil moisture conservation.

sorghum.rationale: Sorghum + Pigeonpea (2:1 ratio) is the premier semi-arid intercrop system maximizing land equivalent ratio (LER > 1.25).
Sorghum + Soybean (4:2 ratio) maintains balanced nitrogen dynamics and controls Striga weed infestation.
Sorghum + Cowpea provides dual grain-fodder security and rapid ground shading to conserve topsoil moisture.

pearl_millet.rationale: Pearl Millet + Pigeonpea (4:2 ratio) stabilizes yield against erratic rainfall in dry semi-arid belts.
Pearl Millet + Cluster Bean (Guar) combines deep taproot legume moisture mining with fibrous millet roots.
Pearl Millet + Cowpea improves protein yield and reduces soil surface evaporation via dense early mulch.

cassava.rationale: Cassava + Groundnut (1:3 alley ratio) utilizes open interspaces during early 75 days before cassava canopy closure.
Cassava + Cowpea provides short-cycle pulse return while fixing nitrogen for tuber bulk expansion.

turmeric.rationale: Turmeric + Maize provides partial overhead microclimate shade beneficial during turmeric rhizome emergence.
Turmeric + Chilli strip companion system utilizes common raised bed irrigation and fertilizer regimes.

castor.rationale: Castor + Groundnut (1:5 ratio) uses wide castor spacing to harvest groundnut pods before castor branches outward.
Castor + Green Gram provides 60-day early pulse harvest and enriches root-zone nitrogen for castor.

sugarcane.rationale: Autumn Sugarcane + Potato (1:2 inter-row) utilizes wide furrow spacing before cane tillering.
Sugarcane + Mustard provides quick winter oilseed cash flow without impeding subsequent spring cane growth.
Spring Sugarcane + Black Gram fixes nitrogen in early cane furrows and reduces early weed pressure.

wheat.rationale: Wheat + Mustard (9:1 strip ratio) is the premier North Indian rabi intercrop maximizing spatial light and oilseed value.
Wheat + Chickpea (4:2 ratio) provides complementary nitrogen donation and balanced soil nutrient exploitation.

durum_wheat.rationale: Durum Wheat + Chickpea (4:2 ratio) improves grain protein and optimizes moisture mining on vertisols.
Durum Wheat + Safflower strip system harnesses deep subsoil moisture on residual black soils.

barley.rationale: Barley + Mustard (8:1 ratio) provides reliable drought-tolerant rabi yield in marginal soils.
Barley + Chickpea (6:2 ratio) improves biological nitrogen transfer and enhances total digestible feed.

mustard.rationale: Mustard + Chickpea (1:4 ratio) provides excellent aphid trap-crop benefits and symbiotic nitrogen transfer.
Mustard + Wheat (1:9 ratio) maximizes systemic land use efficiency and rabi return.

chilli.rationale: Chilli + Onion (1:2 row ratio) repels thrips vectors and exploits divergent root depth strata.
Chilli + Coriander provides natural insect pest diversion and quick herb return before chilli flowering.

tomato.rationale: Tomato + Cowpea inter-row pairing enriches soil nitrogen and enhances soil microbial activity.
Tomato + Coriander attracts beneficial syrphid flies and parasitoid wasps for biological pest control.

eggplant.rationale: Eggplant + Coriander acts as a companion nectar source attracting natural predators of shoot borers.
Eggplant + Cowpea improves ground nitrogen and suppresses early-season weed development.

potato.rationale: Potato + Mustard companion border system emits glucosinolate root exudates that deter soil-borne pests.
Potato + Wheat relay system enables early autumn potato tuberization followed by wheat canopy spread.

onion.rationale: Onion + Chilli companion cropping deters fungal pathogens and optimizes bed surface utilization.
Onion + Coriander provides fast multi-tier herb returns without root interference.

sunflower.rationale: Sunflower + Pigeonpea (2:1 or 4:2 ratio) provides drought-hardy spatial complementarity.
Sunflower + Groundnut (2:6 ratio) pairs tall heliotropic head development with low spreading legume pods.

safflower.rationale: Safflower + Chickpea (1:3 ratio) pairs deep taproot safflower extraction (up to 2m) with chickpea root nodules.
Safflower + Coriander (2:4 ratio) diversifies early winter returns and suppresses weeds.

sesame.rationale: Sesame + Green Gram (2:2 ratio) provides simultaneous harvest with superior soil nutrient preservation.
Sesame + Pigeonpea (4:1 ratio) utilizes sesame rapid maturity followed by pigeonpea podding.

cluster_bean.rationale: Cluster Bean + Pearl Millet (2:1 ratio) is the benchmark arid legume-cereal intercrop for Rajasthan/Gujarat drylands.
Cluster Bean + Sesame (1:1 ratio) pairs two heat-hardy crops with complementary mycorrhizal associations.

cowpea.rationale: Cowpea + Sorghum (1:2 ratio) enables cowpea vine climbing on sorghum stalks, increasing total forage and grain biomass.
Cowpea + Maize provides balanced nitrogen replenishment and complete soil surface shade.

coriander.rationale: Coriander + Chickpea (1:4 ratio) improves pest deterrence through essential oil volatiles while gaining fixed nitrogen.
Coriander + Safflower provides low-cost spice harvest during early vegetative stages of safflower.

pea.rationale: Field Pea + Mustard (4:1 ratio) stabilizes cool-season grain yield and deters powdery mildew spread.
Field Pea + Wheat (2:4 ratio) enriches nitrogen status of wheat roots and reduces fertilizer requirements.

fava_bean.rationale: Fava Bean + Barley (2:4 ratio) is an established FAO cool-temperate mixture with superior crude protein content.
Fava Bean + Wheat utilizes robust nodulation to donate up to 40 kg N/ha to the cereal companion.

cabbage.rationale: Cabbage + Tomato companion cropping repels diamondback moths through solanaceous aromatic volatiles.
Cabbage + Coriander lures beneficial predator insects that feed on cabbage caterpillars.

cauliflower.rationale: Cauliflower + Tomato reduces insect oviposition on curds through companion olfactory masking.
Cauliflower + Coriander provides early border harvest and insect pest suppression.

okra.rationale: Okra + Cowpea (1:1 ratio) reduces root-knot nematode damage and fixes nitrogen around upright okra stalks.
Okra + Cluster Bean combines two mucilaginous vegetable pulses with identical soil moisture demands.

guava.rationale: Guava + Cowpea green manure alley intercrop enriches orchard organic matter and suppresses orchard weed flush.
Guava + Turmeric utilizes shaded inter-row alleys of young guava orchards for high-value spice cash flow.
